principles.principle: Prefer the smallest change that satisfies the request
Prefer a single source of truth; avoid duplicated rules across files
Ask a clarifying question only when critical ambiguity remains
Focus on OSI specification compliance and business clarity

decision.name: fact_vs_dimension
decision.question: Is this table a fact (measurable events) or dimension (descriptive context)?
decision.guidance: - Fact tables: contain numeric measures, foreign keys to dimensions, event-level rows - Dimension tables: contain descriptive attributes, single primary key, slowly changing - If uncertain, treat as dimension (safer for AI query generation)

decision.name: primary_key_strategy
decision.question: What uniquely identifies rows in this dataset?
decision.guidance: - Use simple primary_key for single-column identifiers - Use composite primary_key when multiple columns are required - Always document unique_keys as alternatives for relationship flexibility

decision.name: source_format
decision.question: How should the dataset source be referenced?
decision.guidance: - Use database.schema.table format when the physical location is known - Use a query string when the source is a CTE or subquery - Never use bare table names without schema qualification

decision.name: field_vs_metric
decision.question: Should this be a field or a metric?
decision.guidance: - Field: row-level attribute used for grouping, filtering, or in metric expressions - Metric: aggregate calculation (SUM, AVG, COUNT, ratios) spanning rows - If it requires an aggregate function, it is a metric - If it is a per-row value, it is a field

decision.name: time_dimension
decision.question: Is this field a time-based dimension?
decision.guidance: - Set is_time: true for any date, datetime, year, quarter, month, or day field - Do NOT set is_time: true for foreign keys to date tables (e.g., sold_date_sk) - Only the actual date values in the date dimension should be marked as time

decision.name: dialect_selection
decision.question: Which SQL dialect(s) should be used for this expression?
decision.guidance: - Default to ANSI_SQL for maximum portability - Add SNOWFLAKE dialect when using Snowflake-specific functions (e.g., TRY_CAST, GET_PATH) - Add DATABRICKS dialect when using Databricks-specific syntax - Only add multiple dialects when the expression differs across platforms

decision.name: relationship_necessity
decision.question: Should a relationship be defined between these two datasets?
decision.guidance: - Define relationships when a foreign key exists from fact to dimension - Define relationships for all direct parent-child dataset pairs - Do NOT define relationships for many-to-many without a bridge table

decision.name: composite_vs_simple
decision.question: Should this relationship use simple or composite keys?
decision.guidance: - Use simple keys when a single column uniquely identifies the relationship - Use composite keys when multiple columns are required (e.g., product_id + variant_id) - The number and order of from_columns must match to_columns exactly

decision.name: metric_expression_scope
decision.question: Should this metric span one or multiple datasets?
decision.guidance: - Single-dataset metrics: use field names directly (e.g., SUM(sales.amount)) - Cross-dataset metrics: reference fields from related datasets using qualified names - Ensure the relationship path between datasets is well-defined

constraints.rule: OSI specification version 0.1.1 is the current standard
All entity names must be unique within their scope
Relationship from/to must reference existing dataset names
SQL expressions must be valid for the specified dialect
Vendor extensions must use valid vendor names from the enum

validation.rule: After changes, run the OSI validator to confirm schema compliance
Scan for duplicate names across datasets, fields, metrics, and relationships
Verify all relationship references resolve to existing datasets
Update examples in 5_examples.xml to match new patterns
